claims.claim: Guatemala has no wealth tax

sources.name: TaxAtlas: Guatemala wealth and property tax rates (2026)
sources.says: Labelled 2026. "Guatemala does not impose a wealth tax"; wealth tax rate 0%.

sources.name: PwC: Guatemala, other taxes
sources.says: Last reviewed 09 June 2026. Real estate taxes "are assessed annually at GTQ 2 per thousand on declared property values of from GTQ 2,000 to GTQ 20,000", at GTQ 6 per thousand from GTQ 20,000 to 70,000 "and at GTQ 9 per thousand on values in excess of GTQ 70,000". No net wealth or inheritance section.

claims.note: PwC's Guatemala pages and quick chart ("NP", not provided) do not address it; TaxAtlas (2026) states it. localTaxes.ts (GT) agrees.

claims.newWording: about 0.2–0.9%, which Decreto 18-2026 cuts to zero on homes 90 days after its 28 August 2026 publication);

sources.name: AGN (Guatemalan government news agency): President Arévalo signs the IUSI reform
sources.says: Dated 28 August 2026. Decreto 18-2026, published in the Diario de Centro América, exonerates from IUSI properties "destinados únicamente para viviendas de uso residencial y uso mixto"; commercial property pays 3 per thousand to Q500,000, 6 to Q1,000,000 and 9 above; the changes "entran en vigencia en 90 días".

sources.name: Consortium Legal: Guatemala's IUSI reform, an analysis of Decree 18-2026
sources.says: Dated 3 September 2026. Decree 18-2026 was published in the Official Gazette on 28 August 2026; the new article 11 makes "properties intended for housing, residential use or mixed use ... subject to a rate of zero per thousand", after a special ninety-day period; income tax changes (an exemption for individuals' real-estate gains) take effect 1 January 2027. Nothing on foreign-source income.

sources.name: Rio Times: taxes in Guatemala for expats (2026)
sources.says: Published September 14, 2026. "Only Guatemalan-source income is taxed"; foreign dividends and offshore investment income "remain outside the Guatemalan charge". The property-tax reform "sets the rate to zero on residential property" and the new rates "take effect 90 days after publication, which is 8 January 2027" (inconsistent with the 28 August publication it also gives).

also: sources: added Consortium Legal on Decree 18-2026 to both profiles
claims.note: Check for a bill: the 2/6/9 per-thousand scale is the law today (2026-11-15), but Decreto 18-2026, enacted and published 28 August 2026, zero-rates homes and mixed-use property after 90 days (about 26 November 2026 by count from publication; Rio Times says 8 January 2027, which does not fit its own publication date). The old wording was right today and wrong within weeks, so it is recorded as corrected with the pending date. Not a portfolio tax; localTaxes.ts (GT) does not model IUSI.

claims.claim: Decreto 6-2026 repealed the inheritance, legacy and gift tax (previously 1–25%) from 2 April 2026, so heirs owe nothing locally

sources.name: LexLatin: Decreto 6-2026, Guatemala eliminates the inheritance, legacy and gift tax on death
sources.says: Dated 26/03/2026. Decreto 6-2026, published 2 March 2026, repeals the Impuesto de Herencias, Legados y Donaciones (Decreto 431), which charged 1% to 25% by value; transfers by reason of death "ya no estarán afectas a impuesto específico"; inter vivos gifts to close family get an express VAT exemption.

sources.name: Revista E&N: Guatemala eliminates inheritance tax
sources.says: "Desde este 2 de abril entra en vigor en Guatemala la derogatoria del impuesto sobre herencias"; inheritances, legacies and gifts on death "están exentas del Impuesto Sobre la Renta (ISR)" and are expressly exempted from VAT.

claims.note: Also the summaries ("repealed its inheritance tax in April 2026") and Antigua's why. The repeal covers transfers on death; the tax's own name includes "donaciones" (gifts on death), so the wording stands. localTaxes.ts (GT) agrees.

claims.claim: US estate tax applies above the $15M exemption (2026)

sources.name: IRS: What's new, estate and gift tax
sources.says: The table "Basic exclusion amount for year of death" has the row 2026: $15,000,000 (2025: $13,990,000). The page says the Working Families Tax Cuts, Public Law 119-21, signed July 4, 2025, "amends § 2010(c)(3) by increasing the basic exclusion amount to $15,000,000 for calendar year 2026". Page last reviewed or updated 03-Nov-2026.

sources.name: IRS: Estate tax
sources.says: A return is required when the gross estate, plus adjusted taxable gifts and specific exemption, is more than the filing threshold for the year of death; the table gives 2026: $15,000,000. Page last reviewed or updated 23-Oct-2026.

sources.name: IRS news release IR-2025-103: tax inflation adjustments for tax year 2026
sources.says: "Estates of decedents who die during 2026 have a basic exclusion amount of $15,000,000", up from $13,990,000 for 2025; the release (October 9, 2025) cites Revenue Procedure 2025-32 and is marked as an archival document.

claims.claim: The public IGSS does not cover retirees (who never worked in Guatemala)

sources.name: Living in Guatemala: Healthcare for retirees
sources.says: Published May 4, 2026, updated October 23, 2026. Retirees who never worked for a Guatemalan employer have no IGSS route, and IGSS voluntary contributions cover pensions only ("los beneficios no contemplan la cobertura de servicios médicos"). Guatemala City private hospitals with 24-hour emergencies: Herrera Llerandi, Centro Médico, Universitario Esperanza, El Pilar. Hospital Privado Hermano Pedro in Antigua advertises 24/7 care. Hospitalito Atitlán offers "the only 24/7 emergency and surgical obstetrical and gynecological care within a two-hour radius".

sources.name: Living in Guatemala: Retire in Guatemala
sources.says: Updated November 7, 2026. Hospital Privado Hermano Pedro in Antigua states "emergencies and hospitalisation 24 hours, 7 days a week"; "IGSS is not a retiree health plan". No travel time from Antigua to Guatemala City.

claims.note: Also Antigua's drawback ("No public healthcare for retirees").
